arguments.promptText: A naturalistic commercial photograph for a British professional vehicle-detailing advert. Portrait composition. One fictional unbadged cobalt-blue rear-engine sports coupe with rounded headlights, smooth curved bonnet, black five-split-spoke wheels and clean dark tyres, parked in a tidy grey UK detailing studio. Low close front-three-quarter camera position: the blue bonnet, front wing, near wheel and spotless windscreen fill the picture. Natural perspective, no extreme wide-angle distortion. The car has just been properly cleaned and is completely dry. Crisp straight soft-white inspection-light reflections show the rich blue paint; realistic glass, rubber and metal, no star sparkles or artificial lens flares. Warm side-window daylight from the left balanced with soft inspection lights. A clean concrete floor, a grey rear wall and a discreet detailing trolley give credible depth. Frame the car prominently, with no large empty ceiling area. No people. No readable writing, badges, number plates, watermarks, captions or graphic elements. This is the clean master reference: consistent body geometry, wheel pattern, blue paint and studio will anchor the later dirty scene, cleaning shot and finished hero film.

Create the opening still of a photorealistic British car-cleaning comedy. Use the exact same blue sports coupe, rounded headlight design, black wheel pattern and grey detailing studio as the reference. Reframe slightly higher and farther back into a close medium two-shot: two fictional adults are clearly visible from the waist up behind the front wing, with large readable faces, and the car occupies the lower foreground. On the left a professional female detailer, 35, with dark hair tied back, an unbranded black polo and black trousers. On the right the owner, 50, with short greying hair, a sage overshirt and grey T-shirt. Relaxed closed mouths before speaking, sincere expressions, no broad smiles or exaggerated surprise. They look down at the car. The car is now heavily covered in physically realistic mottled brown winter road grime and dried tyre spray, opaque across the bonnet, front wing and doors so the blue paint is barely visible. Keep the same body and panel gaps; this is dirt on the blue car, not a brown-painted different car. Windscreen remains plausibly transparent, with grime around its edges. The detailer is perfectly tidy and competent; the owner is ordinary and likeable. Warm daylight from the same left window, natural skin, soft white studio lights. No large empty ceiling. No touching or wiping dirty paint, no hand choreography. No writing, logos, badges, number plates, captions or graphic elements.

Thick white prewash foam covers most of the paint. A black pressure-wash lance enters from the upper right; its nozzle is a sensible distance away and a single wide fan of clear water is just beginning to remove the foam, exposing a narrow clean blue stripe. Realistic water droplets, wet foam flowing down under gravity and credible physical spray contact. The operator stays outside frame: no visible face or extra limbs, just the end of the lance. Soft bright inspection light and warm left-window daylight. This is one simple real cleaning action, not a magical transformation. No dry wiping, scratch marks, badges, text, logos, captions, sparkle stars or graphic elements.
